properties.description: Ruthenium on phosphorus-nitrogen co-doped carbon catalyst

nodes.name: PNC support preparation
nodes.procedure: The PNC support was prepared by pyrolysis of self-assembled precursors under an air atmosphere, in which the phytic acid served as P sources.
nodes.source_text: First, the PNC support was prepared by pyrolysis of self-assembled precursors under an air atmosphere, in which the phytic acid served as P sources.

nodes.name: Ru1/PNC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The Ru metal species was adsorbed on the PNC network and subjected to a high-temperature treatment to obtain the final catalyst. The introduced P displaced one of the pyridinic N atoms, providing an ideal platform for anchoring metal centers and in turn creating the metal-P pairs (previously developed methods with slight modifications).

nodes.name: Ru1/NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The atomic Ru-N pairs (denoted as Ru₁/NC) were prepared via the same procedure without the addition of phytic acid.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH (three-electrode RDE)
nodes.source_text: As seen in Figure 3a, the geometric current density (j_geometric) increases exponentially with overpotential (η), and the Ru₁/PNC exhibits faster kinetics than other referenced catalysts, requiring only 16 mV overpotential to reach 10 mA cm⁻². ... The resultant Tafel slope of Ru₁/PNC is 39.4 mV dec⁻¹ ... the corresponding activity normalized by the electrochemically active surface area of Ru₁/PNC is ∼13 fold higher than that of Ru₁/NC
the resultant Tafel slope of Ru₁/PNC is 39.4 mV dec⁻¹, much lower than the 108.8 mV dec⁻¹ of Ru₁/NC

nodes.description: AEM water electrolysis performance and durability
nodes.source_text: the current densities of 1.0 and 2.0 A cm⁻² of Ru₁/PNC can be reached at cell voltages of 1.94 and 2.28 V (without iR-compensation), respectively ... outstanding durability at a high current density of 2.0 A cm⁻², with an average decay rate of -0.08 mV h⁻¹ for over 266 h

nodes.source_text: the TOF reaches a plateau when the P/N ratio exceeds ~0.7, implying the formation of a new coordination structure

nodes.source_text: the average current density of P-doped Ru/C ... is 2.7-fold higher ... than that of the corresponding unmodified catalysts
the activity of Ru/C was reduced by a factor of 1.6 (j_H/j_D)

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings show Ru elements uniformly distributed across the PNC and NC scaffolds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings also show that Ru elements are uniformly distributed across the NC and PNC scaffolds (Figure 2a and Supplementary Figure 8).

properties.description: Color-coded elemental distribution overview image labeled C

nodes.characterization_summary: AC HAADF-STEM images demonstrate formation of Ru single atoms with typical Ru-P pairs highlighted; average Ru-P distance is ∼0.23 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC HAADF-STEM) was then performed to confirm the atomically dispersed Ru sites... The intensity profiles... present that the average distance of coupled Ru-P pairs is ∼0.23 nm (Figure 2g).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS validates presence of P and N elements on the carbon support in Ru₁/PNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) validates the presence of P and N in Ru₁/PNC, implying the possibility of P/N-coordinated single atoms (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru k-edge XANES shows lower photon energy at absorption threshold for Ru₁/PNC than Ru₁/NC, indicating downshift of Ru valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The photon energy of Ru₁/PNC at the absorption threshold position is lower than that of Ru₁/NC, indicating the downshift of the valence state of Ru₁/PNC (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT k²-weighted Ru K-edge EXAFS shows Ru-N peak at ∼1.45 Å and Ru-P shoulder at 1.80 Å for Ru₁/PNC; no Ru-Ru peaks detected; fitting confirms Ru₁-N₃P₁ and Ru₁-N₄ configurations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transformed (FT) k²-weighted EXAFS spectra demonstrate... a shoulder peak at 1.80 Å appears in the Ru₁/PNC... The coordination configuration... suggesting the predominant Ru₁-N₃P₁ and Ru₁-N₄ configurations (Figure 2e,f).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows new peak at ∼129 eV corresponding to Ru-P bond when P incorporation is sufficient; agrees with valence state downshift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectra... when the incorporation of P is sufficient, a new peak appears at ∼129 eV, which corresponds to the Ru-P bond (Figure 2h).

properties.description: 2D color map of binding energy vs P content

nodes.characterization_summary: Solid-state ³¹P NMR shows new peak at -20.2 ppm in Ru₁/PNC indicating coordination environment with P donor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2i shows three well-resolved signals of PNC... However, the Ru₁/PNC shows a new peak at -20.2 ppm (star symbol), which is the sensitive indicator of the coordination environment with the P donor.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns show only two broad peaks at ∼25° and 42° assigned to carbon substrate, indicating absence of Ru nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is further verified by the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns, where only two broad peaks assigned to the carbon substrate at ∼25° and 42° are observed (Supplementary Figure 7).

nodes.characterization_summary: NH₃-TPD of Ru₁/PNC shows peak shifted to 214°C ascribed to stronger acidity of Ru-P pairs; Ru₁/NC shows peak at 110°C from acidic Ru sites; PNC shows peaks at 99°C and 145°C from P species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the NH₃-TPD spectra, the PNC support presents two peaks at 99 and 145°C... In contrast, a main peak appears at 110°C in Ru₁/NC... Similarly, one peak in Ru₁/PNC was shifted to a higher temperature of 214°C, ascribed to the interaction of Ru-P pairs (Figure 4c).

nodes.characterization_summary: CO₂-TPD shows peaks at 84-87°C from basic N species; Ru₁/NC new peak at 196°C from coordinating N; Ru₁/PNC peak at 243°C indicating basicity of Ru single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the CO₂-TPD spectra, the peaks located around 84-87°C... a new CO₂-desorption peak emerges at 196°C in Ru₁/NC... Ru₁/PNC also produces a new peak at 243°C (Figure 4d).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Ru k-edge XAFS under applied potentials shows pre-edge shift to higher energies indicating increased Ru oxidation state from H₂O adsorption; excellent structural robustness maintained.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ XAFS measurement... the pre-edge absorption exhibited a slight shift toward higher energies... the FT-EXAFS spectrum displayed the excellent structural robustness of Ru₁/PNC (Figure 3h,i).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET areas of Ru₁/PNC and Ru₁/NC are similar.
nodes.evidence_snippet: although the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values of Ru₁/PNC and Ru₁/NC are nearly the same due to the similar BET areas (Supplementary Figures 15 and 16)
